item.title: Dangerous Lane-Cutting and Gridlock at Elmbridge Court Roundabout (Cheltenham Road Exit), 9th September
item.description:
I am writing to you as a local resident to raise an urgent road safety and traffic management issue at the Elmbridge Court Roundabout, specifically affecting the westbound exit onto Cheltenham Road.Due to the ongoing A40 Over Bridge works and the revised three-way signal layout at the Nine Elms Road / Greyhound Gardens junction, Cheltenham Road is experiencing severe evening tailbacks. This congestion has triggered a highly dangerous driving pattern that is paralyzing the roundabout.Drivers traveling from the A40 are regularly bypassing the queuing traffic by using the outer circulatory lanes of the roundabout. Instead of exiting safely, they are cutting across the dashed chevron marking right at the mouth of the Cheltenham Road exit at the last possible second.This maneuver is causing severe issues:Gridlock on the Roundabout: When these drivers stop dead in the active circulatory lanes trying to force their way into the queue, they block traffic trying to reach other exits (such as the A40 West or Barnwood), locking up the entire junction.Accident Risks: Vehicles already established in the left-hand exit lane are forced to slam on their brakes to avoid collisions, creating an unpredictable environment at a high-volume junction.While I understand that "No Merging" signs are not permitted under standard traffic regulations, I urge you to work with Gloucestershire Highways to investigate viable engineering solutions for this specific exit mouth. Potential remedies include replacing the broken chevron borders with solid white lines to make crossing them a clear traffic offence, installing high-visibility directional lane guidance, or placing flexible plastic wands/delineators along the chevron island to physically prevent last-second cutting.This bottleneck is severely impacting the daily lives of Longlevens residents and commuters. I would greatly appreciate it if you could raise this matter with the highways team to explore what safety interventions can be found.

item.title: Overhanging hedge, 9th September
item.description:
The owners need to be forced to cut their hedge back to their boundary so as to stop infringing over the pavement. My earlier report has been ignored and a reply sent to me that the problem had been resolved. This is not the case the hedge is overhanging and interfering on the pavement which is forcing pedestrians to walk out over the grass.
